prose:
A So8res essay argues that Anthropic’s public communication and policy work fall short of its stated concern about catastrophic AI risk. The examined sections contrast interview responses with statements to technical audiences and advocate a stronger effort to slow the competitive race.

The post includes imagined alternative interview answers to illustrate its criticism. Those passages are not actual executive statements and must not be quoted as admissions. Its assessments of motives, policy adequacy and existential risk are advocacy, not findings independently established by this summary. This account covers the examined argument rather than every later recommendation.
highlights: Essay is criticism and policy advocacy
Actual and imagined interview answers are distinct
Quoted interview context was not independently reviewed
Assessment of adequacy belongs to the author
Catastrophic outcomes are risk arguments not observed facts
Recommendations do not authorize changes here
